newsitem.title: FINLAND: Benefon says report gives wrong impression.
newsitem.headline: Benefon says report gives wrong impression.

text.p: Finnish mobile phone maker Benefon Oy said on Thursday an article in business newspaper Kauppalehti, reporting modest sales for its new GSM mobile phone, may give a significantly wrong impression of the company.
"The story on Benefon in today's issue of Kauppalehti may give the wrong impression of the company's situation," Benefon said in a statement.
The story may "significantly distort" the impression of the company's overall situation, Benefon said.

Benefon said the newspaper report had exaggerated both the importance of its recently-launched GSM (global system for mobile communications) phone and the problems encountered in Finland in the phone's test marketing phase.

The article did not pay enough attention to its "well developed market position" on what it said was -- given the firm's size -- still a big export market for analogue mobile phones of the NMT (Nordic mobile telephone) 450 standard.
On Thursday, Benefon's share traded at 90.00 markka, down 4.50 markka, or almost five percent, on the Helsinki bourse, and brokers attributed the fall to the Kauppalehti article.

The share was down from a 15-month high of 125.00 markka set on March 12, a week after the company said it had obtained type approval for its first GSM product, the Gamma phone, launched this spring after months of delay.
Kauppalehti quoted phone retailers in Finland as saying that Gamma sales had been modest after a month on the market. The paper said the phone's success would be critical for Benefon.
Kauppalehti also quoted a Benefon marketing manager as saying that while Benefon's total NMT 450 phone sales were up, the Finnish analogue phone market had contracted with "surprising" speed.
